clue.text: Forfeit, not attack, fish

indicators.note: not says the letters of the following word are taken away from the first word

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing or rage

explanation.surface: An angler forfeits a catch rather than attack it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes F, I and T, scattered in order, from FORFEIT, leaving the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The orfe, or ide, is a freshwater fish of the carp family, often kept as an ornamental golden variety.

clue.text: Birds roll from side to side in swaying sycamore tops

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
tops means the first letters of the two words before it

parts.note: to wallow is to roll about, as a pig in mud or a ship in a swell

explanation.surface: Birds tumble about in the swaying tops of sycamore trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tops' gives S and S, and 'in' puts WALLOW between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows are small fork-tailed migratory songbirds, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Broken arm nursed by blokes he's tailed

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside, as a baby is held in arms

parts.note: blokes means men

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of arm are rearranged

explanation.surface: Men tend a colleague's broken arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges the arm as RMA; 'nursed by' means cradled, so the blokes hold it. The definition is a playful description of a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical sea creature that is half man and half fish has a fish's tail, so he is tailed.

clue.text: Controversial artist with little money, powerless to achieve distinction

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a provocative British artist famous for her unmade bed

indicators.note: powerless means the letter for power, P in physics, is taken away

parts.note: pence are small coins

explanation.surface: A provocative artist scraping by on pennies finally wins acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' drops P from PENCE, leaving ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence is high rank or renown, a synonym for distinction.

clue.text: Plate showing Church of Rome losing half of its members, consecutively

annotationWithheld.why: Plate showing Church of Rome losing half of its members, consecutively (6): CH[URCHOF]ROME, six consecutive middle letters of the twelve deleted. The parse is sound, but every honest wp (del with indicator 'losing half of its members, consecutively', or the removed run as a leaf) is refused by halvedAsDeletion/halfInLeaf, and no halving selection keeps CH...ROME
annotationWithheld.clue: Plate showing Church of Rome losing half of its members, consecutively

clue.text: Cheeky formality — no way

indicators.note: no says the following piece is absent from the word before

parts.note: starch means stiff formality of manner
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A cheeky person scorns stiff formality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes ST from STARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means playfully mischievous or knowing, a synonym for cheeky.

clue.text: One not necessarily looking to buy a tanker without resistance

definitions.text: One not necessarily looking to buy

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first piece wraps the second

parts.note: a bowser is a tanker for fuel or water
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A window-shopper browses a tanker sale without putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside puts BOWSER around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser in a shop looks around idly with no firm intention of making a purchase.

clue.text: Jar from pub, steeped in exotic aroma

indicators.note: steeped in means soaked inside, so one piece goes within another
exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of aroma are rearranged

parts.note: PH is the abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: A jar from a pub soaks in an exotic scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the aroma as AMORA; 'steeped in' means the pub sits soaked inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a tall two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage vessel.

clue.text: 0.25 of a yard by 1.25 yards, being hollow

indicators.note: a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter, here the final one

parts.note: the English ell was an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: A tailor's measurements of cloth turn out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The quarter of YARD taken is its last letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dell is a small wooded valley, a hollow in the land.

clue.text: First of the invading Mohicans changing into outer wear

indicators.note: invading means entering, so one piece goes inside another
changing signals that the letters of Mohicans are rearranged
First of means the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Natives change into their coats as the leader invades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' gives T, 'changing' rearranges MOHICANS, and 'invading' puts T inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a waterproof raincoat, an outer garment worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Crepe woven with article-free Milan fabric

indicators.note: woven suggests interlacing threads, so the letters are rearranged
article-free means the indefinite article a is removed

explanation.surface: Crepe is woven together with Milan cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article-free' takes A from MILAN to leave MILN; 'woven' rearranges CREPE plus MILN.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimplene is a trade name for a thick polyester textile popular in 1960s and 1970s clothing.

clue.text: Tree potentially provides answer — "hard growth"

parts.note: a corn is a hardened patch of skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A tree supplies the answer to a question about a hard growth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says 'potentially' because the nut only becomes an oak if it grows.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak nut has the potential to grow into a whole oak, so it is a future tree.

clue.text: As a most radiant star might be pursued by male

definitions.text: As a most radiant star might be
definitions.meaning: the brightest star in a constellation is given the first Greek letter, as with Centauri
followed by the word male it makes the phrase for a dominant man

explanation.surface: Like the brightest star, perhaps, with a man in pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter labels the brightest star in a constellation and also precedes male for a dominant man.

clue.text: Local party takes Rouen — "alternative backed out" slur

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn
a do is a party

indicators.note: out means the following letters are removed from the word before
backed means the word is read backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A local party seizes Rouen and is accused of backing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the alternative into RO; 'out' removes that from the French city to leave UEN; 'takes' puts it between the local and the party.
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an insinuating remark, an indirect slur on someone's character.

clue.text: Rubbish left out for chauffeur

indicators.note: out means the following letter is dropped

parts.note: drivel means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Rubbish is left out for a driver to collect.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb: to chauffeur is to drive someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To chauffeur someone is to drive them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Work round infected matter

parts.note: O is round in shape
pus is the matter from an infected wound

explanation.surface: Treatment works around infected material.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, Latin for work.

clue.text: One that descended to inspire a physicist to invest money in booze?

definitions.text: One that descended to inspire a physicist

indicators.note: investing money in something puts it inside, so one piece holds the other
this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: ale is beer, booze
p stands for pence, and pp is pence in the plural

explanation.surface: A falling fruit inspired a scientist to put his money into drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Newton is said to have conceived gravity on seeing fruit fall from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit that fell from a tree is said to have inspired Isaac Newton's theory of gravity.

clue.text: Moreover, securing a prisoner with a snake

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so the first piece wraps the next

parts.note: and means moreover, in addition
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: In addition, a convict is locked up with a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moreover' is a single word for a conjunction, not a link joining the pieces; 'securing' locks the second article and the convict inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a very large South American constrictor, an example of a snake.

clue.text: Chanel's chief unfashionably fashionable flaw

indicators.note: chief means the first letter of the word

parts.note: hip is a dated slang word for trendy, so using it is itself unfashionable

explanation.surface: The head of Chanel is fashionable in an outdated way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfashionably' is part of the definition of the second piece: hip is an old-fashioned word for fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A chip is a small defect where a piece has broken off, a flaw.

clue.text: Crossword setter? Agreeable type switching two adjacent letters

indicators.note: two letters that sit side by side in the word swap places

parts.note: a complier is someone who goes along with requests, an agreeable person

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is an agreeable sort who swaps letters around.
explanation.walkthrough: The L and I of the agreeable type change places. The question mark marks the definition as an example: a setter is one kind of compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setters are called compilers, as they put the grid and clues together.

clue.text: Explosive heard burying fighting tanks, missiles etc

indicators.note: burying means holding inside, so one piece goes within another
explosive suggests blowing apart, so the letters of heard are rearranged

parts.note: war means fighting

explanation.surface: An explosion is heard burying weapons of war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive' rearranges the letters as HARDE; 'burying' puts the fighting inside. The definition is a sense of the answer far from tools and nails.
explanation.definitionFit: Military hardware means weapons and vehicles such as tanks and missiles.

clue.text: Affectedly modest object (English)

parts.note: to demur is to object

explanation.surface: A coy English person raises an objection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Demure means reserved or shy, often with modesty that is put on.

clue.text: Utter failure, Jamie's last dessert

parts.note: a bomb is a flop in American usage

indicators.note: last means the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Jamie's final dessert is a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Jamie suggests the TV chef Jamie Oliver, which fits the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombe is a dome-shaped frozen dessert.

clue.text: Nevertheless, can interrupt

parts.note: but means nevertheless
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Nevertheless, it is possible to interrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a noun, a container, not the verb its surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt in is to interrupt a conversation, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Scruffy sitcom character wants new hospital department part

parts.note: Compo was the scruffy character in the British sitcom Last of the Summer Wine
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A scruffy television character wants part of a new hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: Last of the Summer Wine was a long-running BBC comedy set in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A component is a constituent part of a larger whole.

clue.text: Elevated room without energy limits

indicators.note: elevated means raised, so in a down entry the word is read upwards
without means the following letter is removed

parts.note: space means room
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A raised room without any energy limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops E from SPACE, leaving SPAC, and 'Elevated' turns that upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Caps are upper limits, as on spending or salaries.

clue.text: Symbol, which a fraudster might own

definitions.meaning: an image standing for something, as on a computer screen
a swindler might admit, or own up, to the statement that he cons

explanation.surface: A symbol that a swindler might possess.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as 'I con', what a confessing fraudster says; 'own' means admit.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a symbolic image or a representative figure.

clue.text: Topless beefcake poser's wear that hurt?

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a pouch is the skimpy garment worn by a male model posing for beefcake shots

explanation.surface: A topless male model asks whether his outfit was painful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' drops P from POUCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the exclamation someone makes on being hurt.

clue.text: Rocky argued about Penny being a better model?

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another
rocky means unstable, so the letters of argued are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rocky argued about Penny being a better model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' turns ARGUED into UGRADE, and 'about' wraps it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: An upgrade is an improved version of a product, a newer and better model.

clue.text: Leave head's unwelcome visitors outside NEC complex

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: head lice are parasites living in hair

indicators.note: complex suggests a tangled arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leave is granted when head lice turn up outside the NEC complex.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is the National Exhibition Centre, a Birmingham venue; 'complex' scrambles its three letters, and 'outside' wraps the parasites round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence means permission or leave to do something.
